I’m an old hand at this now. I’ve grown crops on this land for many years, and with only 6 mu, I can’t afford to make foolish changes just because someone says a new way is better. Stevia is what I know, and on a small plot like mine I’d rather manage it carefully than spread myself thin. At the start of the season, I’ll keep all 6 mu in stevia. I’ll plant in the usual spring window, after the soil has warmed enough and there’s no real risk of cold damage. Since I have well water, I’m not as nervous as some people if spring rain is short, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate unless the soil is really drying or the plants are at an important stage.

For seedling material, I’ll use the kind that has done reliably here, not chase some fancy new source unless I’ve seen it work nearby. Fertilizer, I’ll use, but not excessively. Stevia needs to establish well early, so I’ll put on a base dressing before planting, then a couple of topdressings after it gets going. I’ve farmed long enough to know that if I get too stingy early on, the stand stays weak and I lose more than I save. But I also won’t throw money around because my household is small and some labor is tied up off-farm. I’ll keep tillage simple, hire a little labor when needed for peak work, watch weeds and leaf-eating insects closely, and expect a decent but not exaggerated yield if weather stays normal.
